$comment: Ovrly contracts 0.3.0-draft (pre-1.0). Every closed vocabulary of the contract, one $def each, so the Android models (#62) map each one to an enum with an UNKNOWN fallback. Removing or renaming a value is a breaking change; adding one is additive but read-side parsers must already tolerate it. The source of each list is named in its description.
title: Enums
description: Definitions only; this file is not a payload schema. Read-model fields (investigation, job, report version, claim, evidence, assessment, capture session) tolerate values outside these lists by mapping them to UNKNOWN, never to a success or finding state. Request fields are validated strictly by the server.

extraction_coverage_status.description: Observation-level extraction progress, never an assessment. Source: services.api.schemas.ObservationProgress.

claim_taxonomy.description: Classification of an occurrence, not a verdict. Source: services.claims.Interpretation.

assertion_mode.description: How an occurrence is presented by its source. Source: services.claims.Interpretation.

speaker_commitment.description: Whether the speaker endorses the proposition. Source: services.claims.Interpretation.

eligibility_reason.description: Extraction eligibility, never a finding. Source: services.claims.Interpretation.

claim_uncertainty.description: Uncertainty preserved from source interpretation. Source: services.claims.Interpretation.

analysis_status.description: Media extraction only. pending awaits observations; partial has usable observations plus gaps; no_usable has no usable observations and no pending modalities; complete has processed the supplied available input. Never a research report or continuous OCR claim.

speech_status.description: Speech-stage progress, separate from preparation and research. Source: backend SpeechStatus.

speech_reason.description: Why speech is unavailable (ASR_UNAVAILABLE reasons follow evaluation/asr_policy.py: the last of the primary and fallback model attempts), or no_speech on a completed result with no recognized speech. An unknown outcome is never resubmitted to the same model. Source: backend SpeechReason.

asr_provider.description: Hosted transcription provider. Source: backend ASRProvider; the RFC-D27 fallback is a second model of the same provider, never another provider.

job_state.description: Persisted job state. Source: backend/services/jobs/states.py JobState. Terminal states only move to deleted; a requested cancellation is the separate cancel_requested flag.

retry_class.description: Class of the last scheduled retry or of the terminal failure. Source: backend/services/jobs/retries.py RetryClass.

investigation_state.description: Coarse investigation state as stored by the intake API. Source: backend/services/api/schemas.py InvestigationState. Distinct from job_state, which is one queue job; an investigation spans several stage jobs.

stage.description: Pipeline stage an investigation or job is at. Source: build contract section 4 and RFC section 13. Intake, upload-backed media_validation and opt-in asr are implemented; later stages remain reserved for the pipeline tasks.

processing_status.description: User-facing progress of an investigation. Source: build contract section 3. Separate from relation and overall_assessment on purpose: failed, cancelled and waiting are never findings, and a finding never encodes processing failure.

coverage_status.description: How much of the eligible media has been checked. Source: routes/investigations.py COVERAGE_PLACEHOLDER (not_started) plus the two values the pipeline will report.

media_speech_status.description: Speech eligibility after media preparation, not a transcription result. Source: backend MediaSpeechStatus.

media_text_status.description: Text remains pending after media preparation; this does not claim any frame was examined. Source: backend MediaTextStatus.

speech_unavailable_reason.description: Why prepared media cannot provide speech. Silence within an existing audio track is not an absent track. Source: backend SpeechUnavailableReason.

source_kind.description: Investigation read-source discriminator. POST /v1/investigations accepts only url/upload; captures are created by POST /v1/captures.

timebase.description: What millisecond offsets are relative to. capture: the start of the live capture session (overlay path). media: the start of the complete shared media file (share path). Source: build contract section 4, decision record 0001.

modality.description: Where a claim occurrence was observed. both means the same occurrence is jointly supported by speech and screen text. Source: evaluation contract, RFC section 13.

relation.description: How one piece of evidence relates to one claim. Source: RFC section 08 and build contract section 3. insufficient means the evidence was read and does not settle the claim; it is not a processing failure.

overall_assessment.description: Per-claim aggregate over its evidence relations. There is deliberately no report-level verdict (decision record 0001: no blanket truth verdict). insufficient_evidence is a finding about the evidence, not about the claim being true or false.

source_inspection_level.description: How much of the source the pipeline actually read before relating it to a claim. Source: RFC section 08 axes.

source_type.description: Kind of publication the evidence comes from. Source: RFC section 08 source identity axis; the list is a first draft and additive.

retrieval_relevance.description: How relevant retrieval judged the source to the claim before reading it. Independent of relation: a highly relevant source can challenge the claim or be insufficient.

retraction_status.description: Whether the source itself has been corrected, retracted or withdrawn since publication. Source: RFC section 08, evaluation coverage tag withdrawn-retracted-source.

correction_attribution.description: Who changed the normalized meaning of a claim after the original extraction. Source: BE-10 (#33) reanalyze with reason correction.

capture_session_state.description: Lifecycle of a live capture session. abandoned: the client stopped sending chunks and never closed the session.

chunk_disposition.description: What the server did with a chunk. stored: first time this (session, seq) was seen. duplicate: same (session, seq) and same bytes as before, original acknowledgement replayed, nothing stored twice. out_of_order: stored, but a lower seq is still missing so the gap list grew.
